name: Nic Carroll
headline: Visionary and Innovative Executive Leader
summary: I've led the whole of information technology as a CIO, CTO, and CISO, and today I lead Information Security and Identity and Access Management at Georgia Southern University. I'm a visionary problem solver who makes sure projects are completed on time, at scale, and under budget. I excel at creating new tools, processes, and procedures, including AI tools that are reimagining how a security department works. Over my career I have deployed more than 100 Google Workspace domains and led enterprise migrations between Microsoft and Google in both directions.

experience.title: Chief Information Security Officer
experience.blurb: Leads Information Security and the Identity and Access Management group, protecting data integrity and operational resilience for 33,500 students and nearly 4,000 faculty across a global campus network. Uses AI tools built in house to reimagine how the security department works.

bullets.t: Led the GCC High research enclave, a segregated Microsoft 365 GCC High and Azure Government environment for Controlled Unclassified Information and export controlled (ITAR and EAR) data, through its CMMC Level 2 assessment, implementing all 110 NIST SP 800-171 controls and achieving a perfect score.

Built a unified dashboard that brings every Information Security and IAM application into one view, improving visibility across the environment and speeding the resolution of threats and vulnerabilities.

Reimagined project management at Georgia Southern University with Reimagine IT: Frame it, Build it, Loop it, Launch it, Tend it. Cross functional teams build a working draft with AI partners in a day and launch in days or weeks, with security and IAM built in, not bolted on.

In less than three months, revamped and rearchitected the phishing and spam defense process, cutting the phishing and spam that reaches institutional email by 95% and reducing the time the team spends on it.

Mapped every tool, account lifecycle, and sign in path across the university and built a phased plan to move from repeated password prompts to signing in once, with Microsoft Entra ID as the front door and a live tracker for every step.

caseStudies.title: Talon Secure: A Perfect CMMC Level 2 Score
caseStudies.challenge: Researchers needed a place to store and work with Controlled Unclassified Information and export controlled (ITAR and EAR) data for DoD, DoE, and other federal research that would stand up to CMMC requirements.
caseStudies.approach: Led the GCC High research enclave with partner Planet Technologies: a segregated environment on Microsoft 365 GCC High and Azure Government with approved collaboration tools, protected storage, virtual desktops, and controlled communication. Translated NIST SP 800-171 into daily practice, leading the implementation of all 110 required controls across 14 families, from access control and audit logging to incident response and configuration management. Drove the documentation, policies, control validation, mock assessments, and evidence needed for a C3PAO assessment.
caseStudies.why: CMMC, the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification, is how the Department of War, formerly the Department of Defense, verifies that the contractors and research partners it works with protect Controlled Unclassified Information. Level 2 requires every one of the 110 security requirements in NIST SP 800-171, checked by an independent assessor against 320 objectives. Without it, a university is shut out of a growing share of defense research. A perfect score shows the controls work in practice, not just on paper.
caseStudies.result: A perfect score from a Certified Third Party Assessor Organization: 110 security controls tested against 320 assessment objectives, with no deficiencies in any of the 14 security categories. Faculty can now pursue larger Department of War grants and partner with defense companies.

quote.text: The assessment confirmed our protections are followed in practice, not just written down.
quote.by: Nic Carroll, quoted by Georgia Southern University

caseStudies.credit: The university's Research Security and Export Controls director credited Nic and his team with taking point on preparation.

caseStudies.title: Reimagined Third Party Review: 4,000+ Products in Six Months
caseStudies.challenge: Departments, divisions, and researchers needed new software, hardware, and extensions approved, but the review process was hard to see into and legal, procurement, and IT each worked on their own.
caseStudies.approach: In my first six months, completely changed the third party review and approval process. Made it transparent to requesters and built legal review, procurement, and information technology systems review into a single path, strengthening vendor risk management and data privacy.
caseStudies.result: More than 4,000 products reviewed and approved, from Chrome extensions, hardware, and applications for the research environment to the tools departments and divisions use every day.

caseStudies.title: Rearchitected Email Defense: 95% Less Phishing and Spam
caseStudies.challenge: Phishing and spam were getting through to institutional email, putting students, faculty, and staff at risk and taking up a large share of the security team's time.
caseStudies.approach: Revamped the phishing and spam defense process from the ground up and rearchitected how email threats are filtered, handled, and resolved, all in less than three months.
caseStudies.result: A 95% reduction in phishing and spam reaching institutional email services, and far less time spent by the team handling it.
caseStudies.metricLabel: Less phishing and spam reaching inboxes

caseStudies.title: Reimagine IT: A New Way to Run Projects
caseStudies.challenge: Projects followed the old way: scope for weeks, build behind closed doors, deliver once, and hope it fits. Every change pulled the whole team back together, and staff were tied to old habits, processes, and tools.
caseStudies.approach: Tasked by the CIO with rethinking how the university builds tools, I designed Reimagine IT, a five move cycle: Frame it, Build it, Loop it, Launch it, Tend it. The project owner builds with university approved AI tools while security, IAM, applications, UX, and academic partners shape the work in the room. Guardrails are set once, up front, and every project has one named owner, a backup, and a shared record from the first hour to the change catalog.
caseStudies.result: A methodology for any project, an app, a process, or anything else, that runs at the pace of a day, a week, or a month. Teams leave Build it with a working first draft instead of a plan, and launch in days or weeks instead of months.
caseStudies.metricLabel: From idea to a working first draft

caseStudies.title: Policy Library: Every Policy, From Need to Next Review
caseStudies.challenge: Policies, standards, and procedures were spread across published collections, with no single view of which were current, which were overdue for review, or where Georgia Southern's policies agreed or conflicted with the University System of Georgia manuals.
caseStudies.approach: Built the Policy Library and a complete process that takes a need to an approved SOP, policy, and procedure in eight steps. A leadership dashboard shows policy health by area, review schedules, revisions in progress, and decisions waiting on leadership. Revisions open the policy as the document itself, with tracked changes, paragraph comments, reviewer verdicts, and Cabinet and President sign offs. Every policy is compared sentence by sentence against the USG manuals, and people can ask questions in plain words and get answers cited to the official text.
caseStudies.result: One place to find, revise, approve, and track every policy. Leadership sees what is overdue and what needs a decision, policies that only restate USG are flagged to retire, possible conflicts are flagged for revision, and every edit, comment, and sign off is logged for audits and open records requests.
caseStudies.metricLabel: From draft to posted policy and its next review

caseStudies.title: Sign In Once: Reimagining Single Sign On and Authorization
caseStudies.challenge: Students, faculty, and staff were asked to sign in again and again. Three different systems checked passwords behind about ten sign in services, and settings no one had chosen added prompts. Students, who mostly use their own laptops and phones, felt it most.
caseStudies.approach: Mapped the whole sign in experience end to end: every tool and the sign in it uses, how accounts are created and removed, and a day of sign ins for each kind of user. Built a phased plan to make Microsoft Entra ID the single front door with the existing campus sign in kept behind it, a separate track for personal devices, quick wins the teams could ship without buying anything, and a live tracker so every step's status is visible to everyone involved.
caseStudies.result: A clear path from two or three password prompts each morning to signing in once: none on a university computer and one on a personal device, with every sign in logged and protected by the same MFA rules in one place.
caseStudies.metricLabel: Instead of 2 to 3 prompts each morning
